lessons.title: Conditionals, wishes, subjunctive uses, inversion
lessons.programRef: Tle — Anglais : conditionnels, wishes, subjonctif, inversion (à vérifier sur le texte officiel)
lessons.author: CastBridge (brouillon IA)
lessons.source: Rédaction originale ; textes d'exemple écrits pour CastBridge ; à relire par un enseignant
objectives: Former correctement les types 0, 1, 2, 3 et mixtes.
Exprimer regrets et souhaits avec wish et if only.
Utiliser l'inversion après un adverbe négatif.
reviewNotes: Subjonctif et inversion : le niveau exigé dépend du programme officiel de Tle ; certaines structures (inversion conditionnelle) sont avancées et peuvent dépasser le programme.
Distinction entre « were » obligatoire et « was » toléré (usage courant) : à confirmer avec les consignes de correction.
Variante américaine : le subjonctif sans should est plus fréquent qu'en anglais britannique ; le programme peut préférer should.

blocks.title: Les conditionnels
blocks.md:
Le **conditional** exprime une condition et son résultat.
**Zero** : If + present, present (vérité générale) : *If you heat ice, it melts.*
**Type 1** : réel, futur possible. **Type 2** : irréel du présent. **Type 3** : irréel du passé. **Mixed** : condition passée, résultat présent.

Après **if**, jamais *will* ni *would* (sauf politesse : *if you would help me*).

blocks.caption: Les quatre structures de base : choisir selon que la condition est réelle ou irréelle.
blocks.alt: Quatre cadres : Type 1, real future : if plus present, will plus verb ; Type 2, unreal present : if plus past simple, would plus verb ; Type 3, unreal past : if plus past perfect, would have plus past participle ; Mixed : if plus past perfect, would plus verb.

blocks.title: Exemples et nuances
blocks.md:
**Type 1** : *If it rains, we will stay home.*
**Type 2** : *If I were you, I would apologise.* (formel : **were** pour toutes les personnes)
**Type 3** : *If she had studied, she would have passed.*
**Mixed** : *If I had taken that job, I would be rich now.*

Autres mots : **unless** (= if … not), **provided / as long as**, **in case**, **otherwise**, **suppose**.

blocks.title: Wishes et regrets
blocks.md:
- **wish + past simple** : regret présent : *I wish I had a car.*
- **wish + past perfect** : regret passé : *I wish I had studied harder.*
- **wish + would** : agacement, changement souhaité : *I wish he would stop shouting.*
- **If only** : plus fort : *If only I knew!*
- **It's (high) time + past simple** : *It's time we left.*
- **would rather + past simple** (sujet différent) : *I'd rather you stayed.*

blocks.title: Le subjonctif en anglais
blocks.md:
Le **mandative subjunctive** est surtout formel : forme **de base du verbe** (sans -s) après *suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose, order* et après *it is essential/important/vital that* : *I suggest that he **be** present. It is essential that she **arrive** on time.*

En anglais britannique courant on emploie aussi *should* : *I suggest that he should come.* **Were** après *if* ou *wish* est un autre emploi du subjonctif : *If I were rich…*

blocks.title: L'inversion
blocks.md:
Après certains adverbes négatifs ou restrictifs en tête de phrase, on **inverse** auxiliaire et sujet : **never, rarely, seldom, hardly… when, no sooner… than, not only… but also, little, only when / only after, under no circumstances**.
*Never have I seen such a crowd.*
*No sooner had she arrived than it began to rain.*
*Not only did he lie, he also stole.*

Inversion conditionnelle (formelle) : *Had I known, I would have called.* ; *Should you need help, call me.* ; *Were I you, I would wait.*

blocks.title: Choisir la bonne structure
blocks.md:
1. La condition est-elle **possible** (type 1) ou **imaginaire** (types 2, 3) ?
2. Le moment est-il **présent/futur** (type 2) ou **passé** (type 3) ?
3. Le résultat est-il à un moment **différent** de la condition (mixed) ?
4. Pour un souhait : regret **présent** (past simple) ou **passé** (past perfect) ?
5. Pour l'inversion : y a-t-il un adverbe négatif en tête de phrase ?

blocks.title: Exemple 1 : conditionnels
blocks.statement: Complete: 1) If I (have) time tomorrow, I (visit) you. 2) If I (be) you, I (not accept) that offer. 3) If he (leave) earlier, he (not miss) the train.

steps.md: **1)** Condition possible dans le futur : type 1 : *If I have time tomorrow, I will visit you.*
**2)** Conseil irréel : type 2 : *If I were you, I wouldn't accept that offer.* (were)
**3)** Passé irréel : type 3 : *If he had left earlier, he wouldn't have missed the train.*

blocks.answer: 1) have / will visit ; 2) were / wouldn't accept ; 3) had left / wouldn't have missed.

blocks.title: Exemple 2 : wishes et inversion
blocks.statement: Rewrite: 1) I regret not telling the truth. (I wish…) 2) He had hardly sat down when the phone rang. (Hardly…) 3) If I had known, I would have called. (Had…)

steps.md: **1)** Regret passé : *I wish I had told the truth.*
**2)** Inversion après *hardly* : *Hardly had he sat down when the phone rang.* (auxiliaire avant le sujet)
**3)** Inversion conditionnelle : *Had I known, I would have called.*

blocks.answer: 1) I wish I had told the truth. 2) Hardly had he sat down when the phone rang. 3) Had I known, I would have called.

blocks.title: Les pièges de la condition
blocks.md:
- **If + will/would** : faux (*If I will go*).
- Mélanger type 2 et type 3 par erreur.
- **Was/were** : en usage formel, *If I were you* (pas *was*).
- **Unless** + négatif : *Unless you don't hurry* est faux.
- **Wish** + would pour sa propre action : *I wish I would* est faux.
- Inversion avec **no sooner** : *no sooner had… than* (pas *when*).

items: Écrire cinq phrases vraies sur vous avec chaque type de conditionnel.
Réviser les adverbes qui déclenchent l'inversion.

exercises.prompt: Associez chaque phrase au type de conditionnel ou de structure.
pairs: If it rains, we will stay home.
If I were you, I would wait.
If she had studied, she would have passed.
If you heat ice, it melts.
I wish I had a car.
Never have I seen such a crowd.
exercises.explanation: Le temps après if détermine le type : présent, past simple, past perfect. Un souhait au past simple exprime un regret présent.

exercises.prompt: If I ____ you, I would apologise.
exercises.explanation: Après if, pas de conditionnel ; au type 2 formel on emploie *were* pour toutes les personnes.

exercises.prompt: True or false: « If it will rain tomorrow, we will stay home » is correct.
exercises.explanation: Faux. Après if, on emploie le present simple : *If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.*

exercises.prompt: Rewrite with « I wish » or « If only »: 1) I don't have a laptop. 2) I didn't revise last night. 3) He always interrupts me. 4) She can't come. 5) We lost the match.
exercises.model: 1) I wish I had a laptop. 2) I wish I had revised last night. 3) I wish he would stop interrupting me. 4) I wish she could come. 5) If only we had won the match.
rubric: Past simple pour un regret présent (1 point).
Past perfect pour un regret passé (1 point).
Wish + could ; If only + past perfect (1 point).
exercises.explanation: Regrets : le temps recule d'un cran (présent devient past simple, passé devient past perfect).

exercises.prompt: Rewrite using inversion: 1) If I had known, I would have helped. 2) I have never seen such a crowd. 3) He had hardly arrived when it began to rain. 4) She not only sings, she also dances. 5) If you should need help, call me.
exercises.model: 1) Had I known, I would have helped. 2) Never have I seen such a crowd. 3) Hardly had he arrived when it began to rain. 4) Not only does she sing, but she also dances. 5) Should you need help, call me.
rubric: Inversion conditionnelle « Had I known » (1 point).
« Not only does she… » et « Should you… » (1 point).
exercises.explanation: Dans l'inversion, l'auxiliaire précède le sujet, comme dans une question.
mistakes: Oublier l'auxiliaire (« Never I have seen »).

exercises.prompt: Read: « The school library is closed on Saturdays. Many students complain. The headmaster has not decided anything yet. »

choices: If the library opens on Saturdays, students would have more time to read.
If the library opened on Saturdays, students would have more time to read.
If the library will open on Saturdays, students have more time.
If the library had opened on Saturdays, students would have more time now.
parts.explanation: Condition irréelle du présent : if + past simple, would + verbe.

parts.prompt: Which verb form is correct? « It is essential that the library ____ open on Saturdays. »
parts.explanation: Après *it is essential that*, le subjonctif demande la forme de base : *be*.

parts.prompt: Complete with the correct form: « Hardly (the headmaster / hear) the complaints when he called a meeting. »
parts.model: Hardly had the headmaster heard the complaints when he called a meeting.
rubric: Inversion « had the headmaster heard » (1 point).
Correct word order and spelling (1 point).

parts.prompt: Write three sentences about the library: one with a wish, one with an « unless » sentence, one starting with « Had… ».
parts.model: I wish the library were open on Saturdays. Unless the headmaster agrees, students will keep complaining. Had the headmaster asked us earlier, he would have understood our needs.
parts.explanation: Unless = if not : aucune double négation.

exercises.method: Choisir le type, puis la forme.

exercises.prompt: If she had studied, she ____ the exam.
Which sentence expresses a regret about the past?
choices: I wish I would listen yesterday.
No sooner she had left than it rained.
No sooner had she left when it rained.
No sooner had she left than it rained.
No sooner she left than it rained.

exercises.prompt: The mandative subjunctive: « I suggest that he ____ present. »
